title: PD-MT242-ProseDiffUi

scope.summary:
GOAL: Render the native prose diff produced by MT-241 in the notes/rich editor as a READ-ONLY block-level diff view with two modes — side-by-side and inline/unified — plus a mode toggle. This is the block-aware prose equivalent of the code diff panel (code_editor/diff_editor_panel.rs), reusing its exact rendering and AccessKit conventions so the two diff surfaces feel identical. It consumes MT-241's ProseDiff (BlockDiff{status, kind, left_node, right_node, left_text, right_text, inline text spans}) and renders through the EXISTING rich-editor block renderer (rich_editor::renderer / reading_mode read-only rendering), never re-implementing block layout.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: NEW module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/rich_editor/prose_diff_ui/ (mod.rs + panel.rs holding ProseDiffPanel + row_map.rs for the block-level synced-scroll map) registered from rich_editor/mod.rs with `pub mod prose_diff_ui;`; one integration/GUI test file. NO backend edits, NO legacy React edits, NO change to MT-241's engine.

DETAILED SPEC (structs, panes, interaction, AccessKit ids):
1. ProseDiffPanel: constructed from two RichDocuments (or a prebuilt ProseDiff) plus an `extension`/instance suffix, mirroring DiffEditorPanel::diff(left,right,extension). Holds the computed ProseDiff, a ProseDiffMode (SideBySide | Inline), and a block-level SyncScrollState. Read-only: no editing, no cursor, no transactions.
2. ProseDiffMode enum { SideBySide, Inline } with a mode toggle button, mirroring diff_editor_panel.rs's DiffMode toggle. Toggle AccessKit author_id: `prose_diff_mode_toggle` (Role::Button, matching how diff_editor_panel uses Role::Button for the toggle because accesskit 0.21.1 lacks ToggleButton — reuse that documented workaround).
3. SIDE-BY-SIDE mode: two read-only rich panes (left = old/base doc, right = new doc) rendered by the existing block renderer. Each changed block gets a background tint keyed by BlockDiff.status, sourced from theme tokens (crate::theme HsPalette — same no-hardcoded-hex rule as conflict_ui.rs and gutter.rs; add prose-diff tint tokens if none exist, do NOT inline hex): Added = add tint (right pane only), Removed = remove tint (left pane only), Modified = modify tint (both panes). Unchanged blocks render untinted. Synced scroll by BLOCK MAP: build a block-level row map (row_map.rs) analogous to diff_editor_panel::build_line_map/SyncRow — a Vec of (Option<left_block_idx>, Option<right_block_idx>) so scrolling one pane maps to the aligned block on the other (Added rows have no left, Removed rows have no right). Pane container author_ids instance-suffixed: `prose_diff_panel#{ext}_left` / `#{ext}_right`.
4. INLINE / UNIFIED mode: a single pane listing blocks in aligned order. Removed blocks styled with the remove tint + a `-` block affordance; Added blocks with the add tint + a `+` affordance; Unchanged blocks plain; Modified blocks render the new block AND show the intra-block inline text diff from MT-241 (InlineTextSpan Equal/Insert/Delete) as inline insert/delete-styled text runs within the block (insert = add tint on the run, delete = remove tint + strikethrough), mirroring how code_editor inline mode marks `+ `/`- ` rows but at word granularity inside the block.
5. CODE-BLOCK diff blocks (BlockDiff.kind == Code): render the block's code with the code-diff styling already used by the code editor (monospaced, add/remove tint) rather than prose styling, so a monacoCodeBlock edit inside a note reads like a code diff.
6. Read-only guarantee: the panel emits NO editing affordances and holds NO SaveManager; it is a viewer. Annotation markers/threads on the diff are MT-244 (this MT leaves an integration seam: a public accessor exposing the aligned block rows + their old/new block indices so MT-244 can attach block-range anchors).
7. AccessKit: panel root author_id `prose_diff_panel` (Role::Group, instance-suffixed on dual mount), toggle `prose_diff_mode_toggle`, each pane container suffixed as above, each changed-block region addressable as `prose_diff_block_{aligned_index}` (Role::Group) so Argus can assert per-block tinting and the block count. Reuse rich_editor::scoped_author_id for namespacing (same call conflict_ui.rs uses).

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read MT-241 prose_diff.rs (ProseDiff/BlockDiff/ProseDiffStatus/InlineTextSpan/BlockMergeStatus) and the real surfaces to mirror: code_editor/diff_editor_panel.rs (DiffMode toggle, show_side_by_side/show_inline, SyncScrollState, build_line_map/SyncRow, DIFF_EDITOR_PANEL_AUTHOR_ID/DIFF_MODE_TOGGLE_AUTHOR_ID, the accesskit 0.21.1 Role::Button toggle workaround, the left/right instance-suffix scheme), rich_editor/renderer/* and reading_mode.rs (the existing READ-ONLY block renderer this MT reuses), rich_editor/mod.rs scoped_author_id, and crate::theme HsPalette tokens.
2. Create prose_diff_ui/mod.rs + row_map.rs (block-level sync map) + panel.rs (ProseDiffPanel, ProseDiffMode, show()).
3. Implement side-by-side: two read-only rich panes, per-block background tints from theme tokens, block-map synced scroll, suffixed pane author_ids.
4. Implement inline/unified: single aligned list, added/removed block styling, Modified blocks show the intra-block InlineTextSpan diff; code-kind blocks use code-diff styling.
5. Add the mode toggle + the MT-244 block-row accessor; register the module in rich_editor/mod.rs.
6. Write the GUI test file covering both modes, all four statuses, a Modified block's inline spans, a code-block diff, and empty/identical-doc (zero tints). Capture Argus evidence (screenshot + AccessKit tree) for each surface into HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT.
7. Update the UserManual in the same change (prose diff view: modes, tint meaning, inline word diff, how to open it).
allowed_paths: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/theme.rs (prose-diff tint tokens ONLY if no reusable diff tint token exists)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (legacy React notes editor is scheduled for REMOVAL by TR MT-261..264; never extend it)
src/backend/** (no backend involvement; diff is client-side)
acceptance_criteria: ProseDiffPanel renders MT-241's ProseDiff read-only in SideBySide (two rich panes) and Inline modes with a working prose_diff_mode_toggle button.
Changed blocks are background-tinted by status (Added right-only, Removed left-only, Modified both) using crate::theme tokens (no hardcoded hex); Unchanged blocks are untinted.

Side-by-side scroll is synced by a BLOCK map (row_map.rs), analogous to diff_editor_panel build_line_map/SyncRow, so an aligned block on one pane maps to its counterpart (Added rows have no left, Removed rows have no right).
Inline mode shows added/removed block styling and, for Modified blocks, renders the intra-block InlineTextSpan (Equal/Insert/Delete) word-level diff with insert/delete styling.
Code-kind (monacoCodeBlock / NodeKind::CodeBlock) diff blocks render with code-diff styling, not prose styling.

Blocks render through the existing rich-editor read-only renderer (rich_editor::renderer / reading_mode), not a re-implemented block layout; the panel holds no SaveManager and exposes no edit affordance.

AccessKit: panel root `prose_diff_panel` (Group), toggle `prose_diff_mode_toggle` (Button), panes `prose_diff_panel#{ext}_left`/`#{ext}_right`, changed blocks `prose_diff_block_{i}` — all via scoped_author_id, instance-suffixed on dual mount with no collision.
A public accessor exposes the aligned block rows (old/new block indices per row) for MT-244 annotation anchoring.
UserManual updated in the same change: prose diff view modes, tint legend, inline word diff, opening the view.
cargo test -p handshake-native prose_diff_ui passes; Argus screenshot + AccessKit tree captured for both modes and all four statuses.
proof_targets: cargo test -p handshake-native prose_diff_ui -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'

Argus evidence: argus.screenshot + AccessKit tree dump of (a) SideBySide both panes with add/remove/modify tints, (b) Inline with a Modified block's word-level inline diff, (c) a code-block diff, (d) identical-doc zero-tint case — stored under HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT
expected_tests: unit: block sync row map pairs aligned blocks; Added rows have no left index, Removed rows have no right index
unit: status -> tint mapping distinct per status and sourced from theme tokens
unit: Modified block emits inline InsertSpan/DeleteSpan runs from MT-241 InlineTextSpan
integration: SideBySide dual mount produces non-colliding suffixed author_ids for both panes
integration: inline mode renders added/removed/modified/unchanged in aligned order
integration: code-kind block uses code-diff styling
negative: identical documents render zero tints and no changed-block nodes
implementation_notes: Mirror code_editor/diff_editor_panel.rs conventions verified 2026-07-21: DiffMode toggle with DIFF_MODE_TOGGLE_AUTHOR_ID, show_side_by_side/show_inline/show_merge, SyncScrollState + build_line_map returning SyncRow=(Option<usize>,Option<usize>), the left/right instance-suffix scheme, and the accesskit 0.21.1 note that Role::ToggleButton is unavailable so Role::Button is used for the toggle (the ACs assert author_id, not role). Reuse these patterns for the prose equivalent at BLOCK granularity.

Render read-only through the existing rich_editor block renderer (renderer/* and reading_mode.rs) — this MT is a diff CHROME layer over that renderer, not a new block layout. reading_mode.rs already renders a document read-only; wrap its per-block output with a status tint.

Theme tokens only (crate::theme HsPalette); conflict_ui.rs and gutter.rs both prove the no-hardcoded-hex rule. If a diff add/remove/modify tint token does not already exist, add it to theme.rs alongside the existing diagnostic tokens; do not inline Color32 literals.
This MT is READ-ONLY. Annotations on the diff (block-range anchors, markers, threads) are MT-244; expose the aligned-block-row accessor as the seam MT-244 consumes. The 3-way merge UI is MT-243.
Argus + AccessKit evidence must show tint distinctness and per-block addressability; capture into the external HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT (never into the repo worktree).

surfaces: ProseDiffPanel Inline unified view with intra-block word diff
code-block diff styling within a prose diff

target_entries: Prose diff view: side-by-side vs inline modes, the added/removed/modified tint legend, the intra-block word-level diff on modified blocks, code-block diff styling, and how to open a prose diff

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Read-only render surface over MT-241's pure diff; it emits no business events (merge/save events are MT-243).
Per-block tint decisions and the block sync-row map are exposed as structured state readable by the visual_debugger for no-context diagnosis of a mis-tinted or misaligned block.
Pure render surface; no long-running child process to liveness-track.

risk_if_missed: MT-241's engine has no operator-visible surface: worktree-merge and notes conflict review cannot SEE block-level prose changes, MT-243's merge UI has no diff rendering to build on, MT-244 has no diff view to annotate, and prose review falls back to the legacy React editor that TR MT-261..264 removes.

risks: RISK-1: Misaligned panes — the block sync map pairs the wrong blocks, so a changed block on the right lines up against an unrelated block on the left and the operator reads the wrong before/after.

RISK-2: Tint confusion — Added/Removed/Modified tints are color-only or too similar, so a colorblind operator cannot tell an addition from a deletion (HBR-VIS regression) or a tint bleeds onto an unchanged block.
RISK-3: The diff panel is accidentally editable (a live editor mount), letting an operator mutate a document from a viewer and corrupt state, or holding a SaveManager it should not.
RISK-4: The intra-block word diff on a Modified block is dropped or rendered as plain text, so the operator sees 'modified' with no indication of WHAT changed inside the block.
RISK-5: AccessKit id collision on dual mount — SideBySide mounts two panes; unsuffixed block/pane ids collide, breaking Argus evidence and keyboard access.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): row_map unit test asserts aligned pairs match MT-241's BlockDiff old/new indices; a mixed add/remove/modify fixture proves pane alignment.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): tints are shape/label-reinforced (Added `+`, Removed `-`, Modified marker) not color-only, sourced from theme tokens; a readability check across all statuses is in the Argus evidence; an unchanged-block-untinted assertion guards bleed.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): the panel type holds no SaveManager and exposes no edit method (grep-provable: no apply_transaction / no draft/save import); a test asserts the rendered content is non-editable.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): a Modified-block test asserts InsertSpan/DeleteSpan runs are emitted from the MT-241 InlineTextSpan data, not swallowed.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): reuse the diff_editor_panel left/right instance-suffix scheme; a dual-mount test asserts non-colliding suffixed author_ids for panes and blocks.

Consumes MT-241 ProseDiff/BlockDiff/InlineTextSpan.
corrections: The prose diff renders through the EXISTING read-only rich renderer (renderer/* + reading_mode.rs); this MT adds a diff-chrome layer (tints + alignment + modes), it does not re-implement block layout.
The mode toggle uses Role::Button (not ToggleButton) per the diff_editor_panel accesskit 0.21.1 constraint; the acceptance criteria assert the author_id, matching that precedent.
